<title level="1" right="Class Feature 1">[Wild Empathy](/Classes.aspx?ID=6)</title>

<column gap="tiny">
**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 128

**Class** Druid
</column>

---

You have a connection to the creatures of the natural world that allows you to communicate with them on a rudimentary level. You can use Diplomacy to Make an Impression on animals and to make very simple Requests of them. In most cases, wild animals will give you time to make your case.
name: Wild Empathy

<title level="1" right="Class Feature 11">[Wild Stride](/Classes.aspx?ID=9)</title>

<column gap="tiny">
**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 166

**Class** Ranger
</column>

---

You move quickly through obstacles, whether they’re tumbled stone, tangled undergrowth, or sucking mud. You can ignore the effects of non-magical difficult terrain. As normal for ignoring difficult terrain, this also lets you treat the hindrances of greater difficult terrain as those of difficult terrain.
name: Wild Stride

<title level="1" right="Class Feature 11">[Wild Willpower](/Classes.aspx?ID=34)</title>

<column gap="tiny">
**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 122

**Class** Druid
</column>

---

Your primal will, like that of the greatest beast, can't be tamed. Your proficiency rank for Will saves increases to master. When you roll a success at a Will save, you get a critical success instead.
name: Wild Willpower
